title: evaluate list features with NumPy targets: truth-value and empty-list crashes
answers: mlflow.models.evaluate fails with 'truth value of an array is ambiguous' when features are a list and targets are a NumPy array
evaluate with an empty list as evaluation data raises IndexError
list features with multi-element numpy targets crash in evaluate
convert_data_to_mlflow_dataset list input IndexError or ValueError
body:
Symptom: mlflow.models.evaluate with list features and multi-element NumPy targets fails with "The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous"; empty list evaluation data fails with IndexError.
Root cause: mlflow/data/evaluation_dataset.py:convert_data_to_mlflow_dataset indexes data[0] without checking for an empty list, and tests `targets` for truthiness, which is ambiguous for a multi-element np.ndarray.
Fix pattern: guard the first-element check with `data and not isinstance(data[0], ...)` and test `targets is not None` before calling np.array(targets).
Constraints: this covers only the list branch of convert_data_to_mlflow_dataset; the np.ndarray branch is untouched. Empty data is not special-cased as valid. It falls through to the standard evaluation-dataset validation (the '2-dimensional' error), as tests/data/test_evaluation_dataset.py:test_convert_empty_list_uses_standard_evaluation_dataset_validation asserts.
applies: Input normalization in mlflow/data/evaluation_dataset.py for list-typed data and targets; any new list-handling branch there should follow the same guards.
says: Evaluating a model crashes with an ambiguous truth value error when targets contain multiple elements.
Running model evaluation on an empty dataset causes an unexpected index crash.
Model evaluation should handle list formatted inputs alongside multi dimensional target arrays cleanly.
Model evaluation fails with an error instead of standard validation when input data is empty.
search: In mlflow/data/evaluation_dataset.py:convert_data_to_mlflow_dataset, list-typed inputs must guard data[0] against empty lists and check targets is not None before converting targets with np.array. This prevents truth-value ambiguity errors on multi-element numpy targets and index errors on empty input lists during mlflow.models.evaluate. The rule applies strictly to the list-handling branch without altering the np.ndarray branch, allowing empty inputs to fall through to standard evaluation dataset validation.
